title: palcheck keys the banner-rect expectation on a whole-file substring scan of demos/juice.dem — comment prose matches and read errors are silently swallowed
evidence:
harness/palcheck.odin:161-165:
		y_base: i32 = 10
		dem, derr := os.read_entire_file_from_path("demos/juice.dem", context.temp_allocator)
		if derr == nil && strings.contains(string(dem), "health on") {
			y_base = 10 + rnd.HEALTH_CARD_H + 6
		}
Context read: the matched token is a demo VERB — demos/health_lose.dem:18 is exactly "health on" — but strings.contains scans the whole file including '#' comments; demos/juice.dem:6-7 is prose one edit from matching: "# forecast counting down); 65000ms = the surge moment. The health meter is" / "# DELIBERATELY off: on this richer map the surge drains the meter to terminal"
detail: The gate's banner-rect expectation is keyed on a whole-file substring, so demo prose containing "health on" flips y_base, and an unreadable/missing demo silently defaults y_base=10 (derr ignored). Spurious gate failures only — never a false pass.
recommended_fix: Match only verb lines: strip '#' comment lines (or anchor the match at line start) before testing "health on", and treat derr != nil as a setup failure (exit 2) like the missing-goldens path above it.
